# tabnas — full text for language models

> tabnas is a polyglot parser engine. You describe a language once as a grammar
> and get a working parser that builds a small, uniform `{ rule, src, kids }`
> syntax tree — the same grammar and the same tree in TypeScript and Go.
> TypeScript is canonical; Go tracks it exactly, verified against shared
> fixtures. Grammars can be hand-written or compiled from RFC 5234 ABNF. Open
> source (MIT), sponsored by Voxgig. Site: https://tabnas.dev

## What tabnas is

A grammar in tabnas is not turned into generated code — the grammar *is* the
parser. Install a grammar package (or compile ABNF at runtime) and it parses
input directly. You can inspect a live grammar, render it back to ABNF, or draw
it as a railroad diagram.

"tabnas" is Irish — *Tábla na nAistrithe*, "a table of translations." A grammar
is exactly that: a table that turns one form into another.

## Quickstart (TypeScript)

Install:

    npm install @tabnas/parser @tabnas/abnf

Define a grammar in ABNF and parse:

    import { Tabnas } from '@tabnas/parser'
    import { abnf } from '@tabnas/abnf'

    const tn = new Tabnas({ plugins: [abnf] })
    tn.abnf(`
      add = NR [ PL add ]
      PL  = "+"
    `)

    tn.parse('1+2+3')
    // => { rule: 'add', src: '1+2+3', kids: [ { rule: 'PL', src: '+', kids: [] }, ... ] }

`NR` is the built-in number token; `[ ... ]` is optional; a rule may refer to
itself. The Go path mirrors this via `github.com/tabnas/parser/go`.

## The syntax tree

Every parse yields the same shape:

    { rule: string, src: string, kids: Node[] }

so walkers, actions, and tooling written once apply to every grammar.

## ABNF notes

- RFC 5234 dialect: `=` and `/` (not `::=`).
- Built-in tokens by bareword: `NR` (number), plus core rules like `ALPHA`,
  `DIGIT`.
- Left recursion is accepted and rewritten (Paull's algorithm): `P = P a / b`
  becomes `P = b *(a)`. A purely left-recursive rule (no base branch) is an
  error.
- Actions attach via `@ref` references (e.g. `'@add:o:NR'`).

## Packages

Core (npm `@tabnas/<name>`, Go `github.com/tabnas/<name>/go`):

- parser — the engine.
- abnf — compile RFC 5234 ABNF into a working grammar.
- debug — inspect a live grammar; describe it or render it back to ABNF.
- json — a complete JSON grammar.
- railroad — draw railroad (syntax) diagrams from a grammar.

Plugins: jsonic, yaml, csv, and more — see https://github.com/tabnas.

## For agents

- Constrain LLM output to a grammar, then parse the response — malformed output
  fails at a known position instead of corrupting downstream state.
- Parse agent DSLs / tool-call syntaxes identically in TS and Go.
- Every package ships tested, runnable README examples (`// =>` assertions are
  executed in CI).
- Machine-readable index: https://tabnas.dev/llms.txt
